result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of residential row houses with continuous sidewalks and marked crosswalks at the intersection. While basic infrastructure is present, safety is reduced by parked vehicles obstructing sightlines and a lack of visible traffic control devices.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk limit the visibility between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right-hand curb approaching the intersection

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs or signals are visible to regulate vehicle priority at this marked crossing.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing parallel line markings to continental or ladder patterns to increase visibility.

result.summary: The image shows an urban intersection in a mixed-use area with row houses and a corner store. hazards.description: Vehicles parked right up to the crosswalk edge block sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Intersection
hazards.description: No visible stop signs or traffic signals are present to regulate vehicle flow at the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting trees along the sidewalk to provide a physical buffer and create a vertical sense of enclosure that naturally slows traffic.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, curb ramps, and marked crosswalks within a residential setting. However, safety is limited by parked vehicles obstructing sightlines at the corner and the absence of high-visibility markings or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: A white truck and other vehicles are parked very close to the intersection, blocking the sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching drivers.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk markings are worn and lack high visibility, making the crossing less apparent to motorists.

hazards.name: Open Storm Drain Hazard
hazards.description: A large, open-style storm drain inlet is located directly adjacent to the curb ramp, posing a potential trip hazard or risk for small wheels.
